newsitem.title: USA: Indiana expects arena to survive legal challenge.
newsitem.headline: Indiana expects arena to survive legal challenge.

text.p: Indianapolis' chief legal counsel said Wednesday city officials are confident a new law aiding financing of $50 million of bonds for an Indiana Pacers basketball arena downtown will withstand a legal challenge the state treasurer filed this week.
"We are confident the lawsuit will not succeed," said Stephen Carter, counsel to the Indianapolis and Marion County combined government.
The bonds brought into question by the lawsuit will not be sold right now, but the challenge could cause difficulties if it continues into October when the debt may be issued, Carter said.

Republican Treasurer Joyce Brinkman contended in a Marion County Superior Court lawsuit that the law creating the special professional sports development district unconstitutionally included the establishment of a local bond bank in Lawrenceburg and authorized an annexation.
Brinkman said she did not oppose the arena plans, but believed the grouping violated the state constitution's requirement of a single subject matter and prohibition against special legislation.
The lawsuit names Gov. Frank O'Bannon and state officials as defendants, but the Indianapolis City-County council likely will seek to intervene in the case, Carter said.
Carter said Brinkman's "apparent" problem with the Lawrenceburg portion of the law should not affect the arena financing provision.

The Indiana Supreme Court has upheld similar legislation in the past and the lawsuit is not expected to inhibit construction of the new arena scheduled to open in fall 1999, O'Bannon spokesman Phil Bremen said.
"No one seriously expects a problem there," Bremen said.
Indiana lawmakers last month approved the law creating the professional sports development district in Indianapolis as part of the financing for the $175 million arena.

The Indianapolis City-County council voted Monday night to approve the district, which will capture up to $5 million of sales and income tax revenues annually to back $50 million of bonds for the arena.
The lawsuit assigned to Judge Cynthia Ayers had not yet been scheduled for a court date on Wednesday, a court clerk said.

The arena financing package also includes a $4.7 million infrastructure grant, $9.3 million of restricted reserves from the Capital Improvement Board and $7 million in revenues from the Circle Centre Mall designated for downtown development.
The Pacers owners will provide $57 million and 16 Circle Centre Mall investors have pledged $3.7 million of annual revenues for debt service on $37 million of bonds.
Eli Lilly & Co has pledged the use of land adjacent to the arena site valued at $10 million for parking and construction staging.
